goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 — [P2, confidence 75] `@include flexbox();` makes the action button a flex item while the unchanged `button { float: right; }` at line 306 is ignored for flex items, so small-action controls render directly after the description instead of at the right edge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `.small-action` at line 264 adds `@include flexbox()` which makes it a flex container. The finding claims there's a `button { float: right; }` at line 306 that would be ignored for flex items. Looking at the diff, line 306 area shows `.small-action-desc` changes but the diff doesn't show the button styling. However, the diff does show removal of float-based positioning (like `float: left` removed from `.title` in header.scss, `float: right` removed from `.panel`). The finding is plausible - when a container becomes a flex container, float properties on children are ignored. But I cannot verify from this diff alone that there's a `button { float: right; }` rule at line 306 since that line isn't shown in the diff context. The diff only shows up to around line 300-306 area with `> p { margin: 0; }` changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:277 — [P2, confidence 75] The unrelated `.small-action-desc { padding: 0 1.5%; }` rewrite changes topic activity-feed spacing for every small action even though the stated task only authorizes header-layout optimization, so users receive an unrequested layout change that cannot be traced to the requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this change is 'unrelated' and 'unrequested' based on an assumed 'stated task' about header-layout optimization. However, the diff shows comprehensive flexbox layout changes across multiple files including header.scss, topic-post.scss, topic.scss, and badges.css.scss. The changes to .small-action-desc are part of a broader flexbox refactoring effort (the parent .small-action now uses flexbox), making the padding adjustment a necessary part of the layout change, not an unrelated modification. The finding incorrectly assumes scope limitations that cannot be verified from the diff itself.
